EXECUTION RESEARCH / 01

ExecutionLab

One trading decision. Four ways to execute it. Measure what happens between an idea and a fill.

Completion through time

Cumulative filled quantity as a percentage of the parent order. Unfilled quantity stays unfilled at the deadline.

Execution scorecard

Lower shortfall is better for this replay. Negative means favorable execution or price movement, not a profitable trading strategy.

MethodFilledAverage priceFeesUnfilled costShortfall (bps)

Cost decomposition

Execution cost + fees + terminal opportunity cost = implementation shortfall. Opportunity cost marks unfilled quantity to the final midpoint; it is not a liquidation or a guaranteed fill.

TimeTypeQuantityPriceFee

Model and data

Market orders consume at most one displayed touch per event, with an explicit adverse impact charge. Passive orders use a queue proxy, later aggressor-side prints, post-only rejection, and a fixed cancellation timeout. Event timestamps define quote/print observations, not a full exchange feed.

Replay cannot reconstruct hidden liquidity, precise exchange priority, cancellations ahead of an order, or the market's response to your trading. Depth is assumed refreshed between events. Synthetic fixtures are engineering experiments, not historical evidence. Imported files are user-supplied and are not independently authenticated.

Research beyond the demo

Run independent days and symbols, separate development from evaluation, and compare paired cost differences with completion rates. The included stress study varies fees, delay, queue assumptions, and order size. None of those parameters are calibrated to an exchange.

References: CME transaction cost analysis · IBKR TWAP · IBKR volume participation. The implementations here are educational models, not replicas of broker algorithms.
